evidence.title: Present-day stellar constraints leave multiple high-energy histories for TOI-700 and LHS 1140
evidence.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
evidence.author: Zhang, Yuzhan
excerpts: Abstract Atmospheric evolution on temperate planets records integrated X-ray, extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) and stellar-wind forcing, whereas host stars are usually characterized from present-day measurements.
Rotation and activity histories can converge at late ages, leaving different cumulative exposures compatible with similar current states.
We quantify this inverse problem for TOI-700 and LHS 1140 without treating either planet as a calibrated atmospheric chronometer.
Among rotation-conditioned tracks, 194 histories matching TOI-700 span only a factor 1.077 in current EUV but factors 2.65 and 2.73 in cumulative EUV and wind exposure.
For LHS 1140, 97 rotation-matched histories span 1.0085 in current EUV but 1.567 and 1.543 cumulatively.
An independent X-ray measurement tests the present-activity mapping yet provides little ranking of these histories because their native current X-ray luminosities differ by only 0.0038 dex.

The results separate present-state admissibility, forward-model adequacy and historical identification, and show why an additional present observable need not reduce uncertainty in the historical forcing relevant to planetary evolution.

evidence.title: Use the Transit and Radial Velocity Methods to Detect Exoplanet LHS 1140 b
evidence.author: Wang, Kecheng
excerpts: With the trend of technology advancement and environmental resource depletion, scientists make a hard effort to explore exoplanets that have ideal conditions for new colonization.
Although the telescope becomes innovative, it is capable of detecting longer expansion of space.
However, farther planets need to use some methods, typically, the transit method and the radial velocity method.
By using the radial velocity method, this research applies the data of radial velocity and the mass of the star to calculate the mass of the planet using a formula.
Thus, the topic of this essay is to use both methods to show how they can detect exoplanets’ mass and the location of revolving orbits.
After that, the difference between the two methods needs to be determined because of the differences.
Also, the implications of the radial velocity method are significant.
Specifically, by using the data including the mass of the host star LSH 1140, the orbiting period of LHS 1140 b, also the radial velocity of LHS 1140 b, to deduce the mass of this exoplanet.
The MEarth Project has discovered a rocky planet with aperiod of 24.73 days residing in the habitable zone of the nearby, spun- downstar LHS 1140.
We seek to detect the high energy emission from LHS 1140 in orderto constrain atmospheric escape and aid future studies of LHS 1140bsatmosphere, which are already planned in the JWST GTO program.
In addition, LHS1140 is representative of the low mass, slowly rotating population of M dwarfsin the Milky Way.
A deep X-ray exposure on this extremum of the stellarpopulation will shed insight into the magnetic dynamo and high energy processes ongoing in these stars.

XMM-Newton is ESAs second cornerstone of the Horizon 2000 Science Programme.
It carries 3 high throughput X-ray telescopes with an unprecedented effective area, and an optical monitor, the first flown on a X-ray observatory.
The large collecting area and ability to make long uninterrupted exposures provide highly sensitive observations.
Since Earths atmosphere blocks out all X-rays, only a telescope in space can detect and study celestial X-ray sources.
The XMM-Newton mission is helping scientists to solve a number of cosmic mysteries, ranging from the enigmatic black holes to the origins of the Universe itself.

evidence.title: Gliese 876
excerpts: Gliese 876 is a red dwarf star 15.2 light-years (4.7 parsecs) away from Earth in the constellation of Aquarius.

It is one of the closest known stars to the Sun confirmed to possess a planetary system with more than three planets, the closest of which is Barnard's Star which is 6 ly away; as of 2018, four extrasolar planets have been found to orbit the star.
The planetary system is also notable for the orbital properties of its planets.

It is the only known system of orbital companions to exhibit a near-triple conjunction in the rare phenomenon of Laplace resonance (a type of resonance first noted in Jupiter's inner three Galilean moons).
It is also the first extrasolar system around a normal star with measured coplanarity.
While planets b and c are located in the system's habitable zone, they are giant planets believed to be analogous to Jupiter.

evidence.title: List of smallest known stars
excerpts: This is a list of the smallest known stars, brown dwarfs and stellar remnants, sorted by increasing size.

The list is divided into sublists, and contain notable objects up to 350,000 km in radius, or 0.50 R☉, as well as all red dwarfs smaller than 0.1 R☉ and all neutron stars with accurately measured radii.
